subject: Physics
question: Monochromatic light of wavelength 630 nm passes through two slits 0.50 mm apart. The fringes are observed on a screen 2.0 m away. Calculate the fringe spacing.
response_text:
Given: $\lambda = 630\ \text{nm} = 6.3 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{m}$, $d = 0.50\ \text{mm} = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{m}$, $D = 2.0\ \text{m}$.

$$s = \frac{\lambda D}{d} = \frac{6.3 \times 10^{-7} \times 2.0}{5.0 \times 10^{-4}} = 2.52 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{m}$$

The bright fringes are about 2.5 mm apart, which is large enough to measure with a ruler if several fringe spacings are measured together.
